name: button-group
title: Button Group
description: Button Group component documentation for Tremplin.
lead: Group related button actions horizontally, vertically, or in a wrapping toolbar.

variants.title: Structural styles and dividers
variants.description: Use real solid, outline or subtle variants. btn-group-divider paints separators between adjacent controls in either orientation.

variants.title: Group sizes
variants.description: Set xs, sm or lg on each group; the button size generator applies tokens to its direct button-like children. The unmodified group uses the default size.

variants.title: Native checkbox group
variants.description: Each real checkbox can be selected independently. Put the input inside its btn-check label; no Button plugin or invented group controller is needed.

variants.title: Native radio group
variants.description: Same-name native radios select one value. Native radio keyboard behavior is separate from Button pressed-state toggles.

variants.title: Toolbar and input group
variants.description: The toolbar wraps separate groups and a named input group. Its CSS does not implement an editor or roving tabindex.
variants.markup: Page

variants.title: Nested Menu
variants.description: A nested group keeps the join geometry. The named native trigger uses the real Menu data API; group CSS alone does not open or manage the menu.
variants.markup: InstallationMenu guide

variants.title: Vertical group and links
variants.description: Vertical groups share edge rounding and optional separators. Link groups remain navigation, with a real current destination.
variants.markup: GroupsButtons

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Logical seams and edge radii follow direction. The inverse theme is chosen deliberately for readable controls.

keyboard.behavior: Follow native controls in DOM order; group CSS provides no roving tabindex.
Activate native buttons; Space changes native checkbox state. Links retain native Enter navigation.
Native same-name radios supply their browser keyboard behavior. Menu has its own arrow/Escape policy when initialized.

guidelines: Give groups and toolbars meaningful labels and the appropriate group or toolbar role.
Use structural button variants on direct children so the join and sizing selectors match.
Configure sizes on every nested group separately; native inputs inside btn-check labels retain checked semantics.
Button groups have no independent token map; customize their button tokens before the button module is loaded.
Menu behavior belongs to Menu JavaScript. Split-menu patterns are not supported in vertical groups.
Keep DOM order meaningful; use native disabled or deliberately guard/remove a disabled link destination.

javascript: Button group layout is CSS-only. Native checkbox and radio examples need no group plugin; the nested Menu example requires Menu JavaScript.

name: close-button
title: Close Button
description: Close Button component documentation for Tremplin.
lead: Provide a named close control and connect it to an explicit action.

variants.title: Disabled state
variants.description: Native disabled blocks user activation; the pinned CSS reduces opacity and suppresses pointer interaction.
variants.markup: <button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Unavailable close action" disabled></button>

variants.title: Dismiss an alert
variants.description: The Alert data API removes this alert. The icon class alone has no action, and application code must arrange suitable focus after removal.
variants.markup: A dismissible example.

variants.title: Size and opacity tokens
variants.description: Customize actual close-control tokens on the control. Leave its content empty; do not add a second text glyph.
variants.markup: <button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close larger example" style="--trm-btn-close-size: 1.5rem; --trm-btn-close-opacity: .8"></button>

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: The mask paints with the inherited foreground. Set a suitable local background and foreground as well as the theme; do not assume that theme alone inverts every icon.

keyboard.behavior: Focus an enabled native button. Native disabled removes it from keyboard activation.
Run the assigned action; dismissal needs the corresponding component data API or application handler.

guidelines: Provide an accessible name for every icon-only control and specify type="button".
Keep btn-close empty: its SVG CSS mask is painted with currentColor, not injected pseudo-text.
A standalone example demonstrates the control; it does not close the page or invent an overlay controller.
Use the correct data-trm-dismiss target for the owning component; focus restoration is not a close-button CSS feature.
Custom mask data URLs require an appropriate image CSP; this is separate from the calendar external SVG asset policy.

javascript: The close icon is CSS-only and has no action by itself. The dismissible Alert example requires Alert JavaScript; application code arranges suitable focus after removal.

name: nav
title: Nav
lead: Style ordinary navigation separately from panel-switching Tab behavior.

variants.title: List markup and disabled destinations
variants.description: Keep the list inside a named navigation landmark. aria-current identifies the current page; the disabled example has no href and is removed from the tab order.
variants.markup:
• Nav
  • Tab plugin
  • Unavailable destination

variants.title: Tabs appearance
variants.description: nav-tabs changes appearance only. These are navigation links, not a tablist or a panel-switching widget; use the Tab plugin for that behavior.
variants.markup: OverviewCardsButtons

variants.title: Pills
variants.description: Pills compose a real theme for the selected background and contrast foreground. The inverse theme avoids relying on an untested semantic color pair.
variants.markup: OverviewCardsButtons

variants.title: Vertical pills and underline
variants.description: Use the dedicated vertical-pill modifier, or compose a flex direction on an underline navigation.
variants.markup:
OverviewCardsButtons
OverviewCardsButtons

variants.title: Fill and justify
variants.description: Fill grows items in proportion to their contents; justified links have equal flex bases. Neither class supplies a navigation controller.
variants.markup:
OverviewLonger installation guide
OverviewLonger installation guide

variants.title: Responsive alignment
variants.description: Responsive prefix utilities switch the column to a row at sm. Nav already wraps; logical alignment follows document direction.
variants.markup: OverviewCardsButtons

variants.title: Navigation with a Menu
variants.description: An ordinary navigation can contain a named Menu trigger. Menu JavaScript supplies opening, keyboard behavior and dismissal; no tab roles are added to navigation links.
variants.markup:
Nav guide
InstallationMenu guide

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Logical layout and inherited tokens adapt to the local theme and direction.
variants.markup: OverviewCardsButtons

keyboard.behavior: Follow enabled native links and controls; ordinary navigation is not a roving-focus tab widget.
Follow a focused link. Native buttons retain their own activation semantics.
Only an initialized Menu or Tab widget supplies its corresponding keyboard policy; nav CSS does not.

guidelines: Name navigation landmarks and identify current destinations with aria-current.
Do not put navigation roles on the list itself or ARIA tab roles on ordinary links, even when styled as tabs.
A disabled class or aria-disabled is not an activation guard; deliberately remove or guard a disabled destination.
Use the actual Tab plugin and its selected/panel semantics for dynamic tabbed regions.
Menus require Menu JavaScript. Keep their owning trigger and menu names explicit.
Verify long links at narrow widths. Wrapping does not break a single nowrap link into words.

example: OverviewCardsButtons
javascript: Nav styles and ordinary navigation links are CSS-only. The Menu example requires Menu JavaScript; dynamic tab panels require the separate Tab plugin.
